incidents.title: 'No Kings' Nationwide Protest — Trump's 80th Birthday (Austin Watch)
incidents.location: Austin State Capitol / Congress Ave / Downtown (2,000+ national locations)
incidents.detail: The 'No Kings' movement is holding its fourth large-scale national mobilization today, timed to President Trump's 80th birthday. Over 2,000 locations nationwide registered, organized by 50501, Indivisible, and the Committee for the First Amendment. Today's format is hybrid/cultural — primary anchor is a 90-minute livestream concert 'Rise Up, Sing Out' at New York's Town Hall, with watch parties and local gatherings at registered sites nationwide. Previous June 2025 mobilization drew ~5 million participants. TODAY'S FORMAT: Organizers describe today as a 'cultural protest' — less street march energy, more watch parties and community gatherings. Generally peaceful. However, counter-protest interaction with far-right groups has produced isolated clashes at past No Kings events, and the Austin Capitol/Congress corridor is a historically active gathering point. White House is simultaneously hosting a UFC cage-fight on the South Lawn for Trump's birthday. AUSTIN SPECIFIC: Austin is a confirmed No Kings location (Indivisible Austin chapter active). Expect gathering activity at or near Texas State Capitol (1.1 mi N). Congress Ave corridor elevated foot traffic. Monitor X and Telegram for real-time Austin event updates. Property staff: maintain non-engagement posture toward political gatherings. If protest activity approaches hotel perimeter: notify security supervisor.

incidents.title: U.S.-Iran MOU — Signing Standoff (Today vs. 'Next Few Days')
incidents.detail: Trump posted Saturday on Truth Social: 'The Deal is scheduled to be signed tomorrow' (June 14). Qatar negotiators flew to Tehran overnight Sunday to assist in finalizing. Iran's IRGC stated via Telegram that Sunday signing is 'absolutely not happening' and characterized Trump's insistence as 'unusual stubbornness.' Iran FM spokesman Baghaei: 'It may not happen tomorrow, but we cannot rule out the possibility of it occurring within the next few days.' A virtual/electronic signing format is the current plan — VP Vance and Iran's Speaker Ghalibaf were originally expected to sign in person but Trump's G7 schedule forced a remote format. WHAT THE MOU COVERS: 60-day ceasefire extension; Strait of Hormuz reopening; U.S. naval blockade lifted; Iran commits to nuclear program dismantlement talks; Iran stops funding proxy groups; staged sanction relief. No cash payment at signing. AUSTIN RELEVANCE: If MOU is signed today, expect Iranian diaspora response (both celebratory and protest) in Austin/UT corridor. Oil prices will drop further. Iranian cyber retaliation risk declines significantly upon signing but remains elevated until Strait formally reopens. Brief all guest-facing staff: WC-themed phishing and cyber threats remain active — do not assume normalized environment.

incidents.title: APD Tasing Death — Body Camera Released; DA Investigation Confirmed
incidents.detail: APD released body camera footage Saturday afternoon and formally identified the deceased as Josh Ryan Trumble, 32, who died June 6 after being tased during an arrest. Seven officers identified and placed on administrative leave. APD Chief Lisa Davis released the footage as part of transparency protocols. Two concurrent investigations: (1) Criminal investigation by APD's Special Investigations Unit with Travis County DA's Office — this is new and significant, elevating community response potential; (2) Administrative investigation by Internal Affairs with oversight from Austin Police Oversight. No charges pending; toxicology pending. COMBINED WITH NO KINGS PROTESTS today: The convergence of a national anti-authoritarian protest day and an active in-custody death investigation in Austin elevates the potential for larger-than-expected gathering at the Capitol/Congress corridor. Exterior staff non-engagement posture. APD non-emergency: (512) 974-5000.
